stats.fact: Apple released the official Safari MCP server on July 1, 2026 in Safari Technology Preview 247, the first official browser MCP integration from a major browser vendor.
The official Safari MCP server ships 16 built-in tools (some report 17), covering DOM inspection, screenshots, JS evaluation, console, network, and tab management.
The server is built into safaridriver — the W3C WebDriver implementation that has shipped with Safari since version 10 on macOS Sierra (2016) — toggled with the new --mcp flag.
MCP is Anthropic's open protocol introduced November 2024 and later donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025.
Apple's Xcode 27 ships a native MCP implementation (mcpbridge), making Safari MCP Apple's second first-party MCP server inside a month.
A community safari-mcp npm ecosystem (e.g. erwinzhang7/safari-mcp, achiya-automation) offers 80+ tools via AppleScript + Swift, working on production Safari, with zero-to-minimal dependencies.

The official Safari MCP server has no access to personal browser profile data (AutoFill, history); captured page content, console logs, and screenshots go directly to the connected agent and its model provider.

angles: First-class Apple support for agentic web development — official MCP from a major browser vendor for the first time
Close the Safari/WebKit blind spot: agents could already drive Chrome but not WebKit, the engine behind every iOS browser
Terminal-only debugging workflow — agent can open site, read DOM, check styles/layout, evaluate JS for performance, and check accessibility without window-hopping
Security/privacy angle: no profile-data access, but page content reaches the model provider — connect only trusted agents; prompt-injection risk
